ABM Nurul Islam with Mahfuzur Rahman with Abdus Salam Mondal and Fara Mahmuda, Advocates — For the Petitioner 
Abdul Wadud Bhuiyan, Additional Attorney-General with Mir Hashmat Ali, Assistant Attorney-General — For the Respondents
parties:
Aminul Ghani Titto (Md) ----- Petitioner
Vs.
Bangladesh Election Commission represented by Chief Election Commissioner and another  ----- Respondent
full_judgment: 6. Mr. Abdul Wadud Bhuiyan, the learned Additional Attorney-General appearing for the respondents, submitted that qualifying date in relation to the preparation, amendment or revision of every electoral roll means the first day of January of the year in which the electoral roll is prepared or revised as contemplated in the Electoral Rolls Ordinance, 1982. It is further submitted that the electoral rolls may be amended, corrected or revised according to sections 10 and 11 of the Electoral Rolls Ordinance, 1982 and a fresh electoral roll may be prepared if the Commission finds therein any gross irregularity under section 7(7) of the Ordinance and any person whose name has not been included in the roll may apply for enrolment under rule 20 of the Electoral Rolls Rules, 1982. It is further submitted that the qualifying date marking a particular date in the year when the election is held is an essential feature of the Ordinance whereby fixing a qualifying date in relation to the preparation, amendment and revision of the electoral roll on the first day of January of the year when the election is held has been done within the legislative competence and hence cannot be held as ultra vires to the Constitution. The learned Additional Attorney-General further argued that in every election previously held in this country and also in the adjoining countries in the Sub-Continent for the preparation of Electoral Roll the qualifying date is prescribed as a component part of election laws. In our country in the past in the Electoral Ordinance, 1972 (President's Order 100 of 1972) and in the Electoral Rolls Ordinance, 1974 and 1976 the qualifying date was fixed on 1st January of the year of election. The Representation of the Peoples Act 1950 (Act 43 of 1950) also contained similar provision of qualifying date in relation to the preparation or revision of electoral roll on the 1st day of January of the year in which the roll was prepared or revised. In this respect a number of decisions was cited by the learned Additional Attorney-General. The learned Advocate for the petitioner found it difficult to controvert the submission of the learned Additional Attorney-General by showing any law or citing any decided case.
